news_items.title: Saints add to their offense and get a hidden need filled with Oscar Delp pick

news_items.full_text: All right, guys. Um, we got two Georgia Bulldogs today. So, quite the coincidence there. Uh, turned out pretty well for us. Obviously, uh, I'll just start with some highlights. Uh, you know, drafting Christian in the second round. Um, you know, four-year player at Georgia. Uh, two-year starter. Um, as we went through this process, we had a formal interview with him at the combine. Um, Peter Surman actually worked him out at Georgia. Uh, funny story there. was supposed to go, but the uh TSA issues at the uh airport kind of created a bit little bit of an issue there. So, Peter happened to be somewhere else close by and he hopped in the car and drove over there and worked him out. And so, uh it all worked out. But great player, love his energy, love his juice. I think you guys already sense that and kind of his media obligation so far. His versatility and his play style is going to be really good for us. And so, uh great move there. And then Oscar Del in the third round. Um you know, we had a formal interview with Oscar at the combine. He kind of shared I think a little bit of that. Josh Hill went and worked him out and so we got exposure to both these guys. Felt really comfortable with that through this whole process. He's a multi- spot guy. He's played a lot of different positions in his career there. He's played with some other tight end so he knows how to kind of play that you know multi-tighten uh type role and u you know that was a great opportunity for us obviously uh you know for him to still be available in the third round was a nice luxury for us and so two really good players to add to this thing and we'll just keep going tomorrow. So, >> coach Bach in line so long he missed his flight. >> Uh, we just had issues with kind of logistics and travel and all that sort of stuff. That was uh that was that Sunday Monday. Uh, you know, a lot of guys had issues with airports with uh TSA issues and so uh a lot of our coaches there's a lot of funny stories associated with a lot of our coaches ended up shifting gears and covering other people and you know some people hopped in cars and just started driving really far away and uh just to connect with these guys. So, it was fun. Was it was these two guys kind of in a bullpen, if you will, at those rounds or did they kind of surprise you when they were there? >> Well, yeah. I think we felt great about both of these guys. Obviously, you're going to get to pick one of them in the second round. Uh felt great about Christian. We're hoping, you know, he was certainly in that clump of guys we're hoping was going to be available for us in this situation. And then, uh, you know, as the third round progressed, uh, having Oscar still available, I think that was a certainly a great opportunity for us just to add to that group. Again, we feel great about our tight ends and now we get to add him into that position and people know the way, you know, this league's trending with the ability to play in multiple tight end sets and that's that's a valuable asset. And so, uh, you know, there's nothing wrong with having a few of those guys that you can play with. >> When you have a guy like Delt utilized in sort of a hyperspecific way at Georgia, what are some of the traits that you were looking for to identify how he might fit differently if used differently in your system? >> Yeah, I think he's got a number of things that will come to the table. Obviously, we recognize the athleticism that he provides. You know, he he does a great job out in space. He's got some juice, some some speed, vertical speed. I think he's a very willing, physical run player. I think that's an important aspect. Certainly, we know um you know, with Jawan and Noah and the other guys we have, like we got some guys who can make some some play with the the ball in their hands. And so, you know, these guys are going to have to do some dirty work and he's ready for that. And I think one of the things that he maybe hasn't done as much, but he'll certainly be ready to do and I think he'll embrace just the special teams component of that. You know, I think uh he's got every trait you can possibly think of to be a really good special teams player. And so I'm excited to see him develop there. >> Is he someone like like when you watch him and then you look at the numbers, like to me it just kind of like he looks different than he does on paper. Like is that a fair assessment maybe of like his receiving ability that there's more there than maybe 200 yards a season or whatever? Yeah, I I think it's it's a byproduct sometimes of, you know, Georgia has a phenomenal formula of playing really successful football and, you know, you can look at it uh with a lot of their offensive players. You know, the receiver room and the tighter room. There's just not going to be as many uh pass catching opportunities in their seasons. And so they do an excellent job of, you know, controlling games. They have, you know, one of the best defenses every single year in in college football. And so, uh, he played with some other guys early in his career. And so, um, you know, he's kind of had this, you know, 20 in the 20s. let's call it. Um, you know, catches per per season, but uh, you know, he does a lot of other other pieces I think that all add to the sum of a really good player. And so, um, yeah, he's got plenty of really good football, some of his best football moving forward. >> Do you think he has like real like two-way ability to to kind of really excel both >> in the running pass? >> Yeah. >> Yeah. Yeah, absolutely. I think uh, you know, he's got some really good versatility. I think, you know, the way they, you know, played him, obviously he played a little bit more of like an off the- ball tight end, uh, in a wing alignment a lot of times, uh, you know, he'll be able to play potentially in the back field on on the line of scrimmage and off the ball. And so, uh, yeah, I think what we're getting is a really smart player. I think he's really he he'll be able to handle some volume and I think it'll he'll allow us to play the chess piece game when you have Jawan and you have Noah and you have these other tight ends that you want to kind of put in certain positions, he'll be able to kind of counteract with those guys. >> Is Josh Hill the right comp for him? That's a great We should We should throw Josh up in the interview process and let's let's ask him. But, uh, Josh felt great about him. You know, Chase, Josh, those guys were fired up. Uh, I think our coaching staff really had a really good vision for, you know, how this guy can play with those other tight ends. And again, um, the value of playing in multiple tight end positions um, is valuable. You know, you can see the teams that made runs this year. A lot of them are playing in 12 and 13 personnel. Um, and we think there's still the pass game juice that these guys provide because of what, you know, those guys have in the pass game I think is going to be a benefit. These guys aren't a bunch of, you know, just big wise. They're just going to block and, you know, when we get in 13 personnel, it's kind of a ding-ding. I think, you know, we can do a lot of things with those guys. >> Do Christian complent each other or will they compete like for one of the same spots like >> No, they they can play they can certainly play on the field at the same time. I think uh you know one of the thing that Christian has done is he's played a number of spots across the front and I think that versatility is going to provide you with some fun chest piece games. Um you know he's certainly played you know plenty of nose but he he'll play the shade. He'll work his way out all the way out to five technique and some three four structures and so um you know he's going to provide some really good versatility and and that group uh it's great to add one to that piece. Uh you know defensive linemen are hard to find in this league and uh he's a talented one. that versatility that did that character just his attitude kind of also like a great selling point of why he went in the draft. >> Yeah, we we had a fun interview process with him and uh you get a little dose of who he is and so uh we're fired up to have him here. I know like all these guys there's a ton of hard work moving forward to you know you got to get acclimated from college to to the NFL. I think coming from a Georgia is a really um beneficial thing for both of these guys. They're as prepared as anyone you can imagine. But, uh, you know, there'll be a transition, but I think he's ready to work his tail off and get ready to go. >> Both of these, uh, players very physical. They talked about in the media availability >> and even your the wide receiver, the Tyson, he loves to block. Yeah. >> Is that the number one trait you wanted this draft? >> I think it's an important trait. Um, >> you know, you got to run the football on offense. We got to stop the run on defense. U, that leads to so many things. Uh, but this game's a physical game and so no matter what position you're playing, uh, we went through with Jordan yesterday, like, you know, receivers got to be physical. They got to be physical in the run game. They got to be physical in the pass game, these corners u are going to press you in this league. They're not going to play off like like college football maybe tends to. Um, you know, then when you get, you know, interior D line tight ends are going to play some dirty work. I mean, there's there's nothing uh easy about those job responsibilities in this league. And so, uh, I think we got really high character guys that are going to do it. >> When I would say that kind of generally You're looking you're looking for guys who can help you in multiple different ways. >> Jordan being able to play all three positions and Oscar being passer. >> Yeah, I think I think that's key. I think uh you know our rosters have a certain size to them and I think it's important that you have guys who can uh provide multiple opportunities to help help the football team. And so uh you know we feel like all three of these guys will have the versatility that they need and you know they'll they'll provide a really good role for them. you get two guys that are teammates in college like this and and like a couple times last year as well. Do you >> just during the pre-draft process, do you talk to them about one another? Do you ever check in like do you utilize that at all? Sometimes during the draft process, we like to ask and prompt the questions of uh Jeff always does a great job with this is you know if you're coming to our organization like who's the culture player that you want to bring you know and then sometimes who's the best player that you want to bring and sometimes it prompts us you know ideas and sometimes maybe we ask who's the best player you played against and so I think anytime you get to collect those different questions get the answers to them uh you collect as much information as you can but uh you know certainly having guys who have a relationship that kind know each other. You know, certainly, you know, Tyler and Quincy last year and we we've seen that throughout this thing. Um, you know, there there's benefits to that. >> Did Oscar or Christian mentioned one another when >> I don't recall. I'll have to look back through our notes. >> Kelly, before you got here, this team didn't used to make all the draft picks up is elite. Um, >> yeah. it has there been a conscious effort for because of the state of this roster to try and and lead with as many picks as you enter these drafts with or have there been a lot of >> I think there's plenty of conversations about moving up constantly. I think it's just a matter of, you know, finding the right value and right situation and, you know, hey, we we've done that, you know, certainly we've had conversations even today about that. Um, but we understand we got great opportunities to add to this team and um, you know, certainly when you look at from this perspective, as many opportunities and swings as you can get, you know, that's a positive thing and for for us, we feel like, you know, we're still getting really talented players are certainly going to help our team. was value kind of maybe one of the reasons why you guys didn't take an edge rush today or anything like that. >> Well, I think there's there's plenty of conversations and still certainly we have another whole day of this. Um, you know, you you get you build a board and you trust your board and you have plenty of conversations as you go and certainly there's conversations and you got to make make decisions. You know, there's guys that we love. There's you know, I think that's the hardest part of this draft is we invest so much time into this process. we kind of fall in love with a lot of these players and then you only get to Yeah, you got to pick one in in each, you know, situation and you got to go and, you know, you're going to miss out on a few other opportunities. >> How much are you guys also weighing that like, you know, all the players that are still available, but also some of the veterans that could be available in the trade market or in the second wave of free agency after like after the draft? How are you going to weigh all those? >> Yeah, I mean, player acquisitions, year- round process. Um, you know, we're going to have obviously an opportunity to sign guys here. Hopefully sign some guys who maybe don't get drafted and then there's plenty of veterans out there that you're going to have continued conversations with. And so, uh, that goes all the way, you know, all the way through training camp in into the season. We know how these things go. And, um, while this is a very, very important part of building our roster and building our team, it's, you know, certainly very well recognized, there's a lot of other opportunities to keep going. Was back Georgia uh influencing your time in Philly at all? >> No. No. But yeah, certainly How's done it a few times. So, >> what do you see as the potential benefits of having um you know, two skilled players in the passing game coming in on the heels of a young quarterback establishing himself as a starter and them kind of going through this together? Yeah, I think certainly we're trying to build a group that hopefully, you know, has some continuity and and works together for a number of years. And so, um, you know, certainly when you look at what Jordan's hopefully going to provide for us, the the connection with him and Tyler and, you know, I think, you know, Oscar has just turned into a great situation. We feel great about our tight end room. You know, to add Noah during the offseason process to now get Oscar on board and to have a number of other guys that we were able to, you know, keep on our roster, we're in a really healthy spot. And you know, I think the more those guys spend time together and and work through this entire OTAA process into the summer program, into training camp, uh there's a lot of time that needs to be invested into this. But, uh, you know, we got the right kind of guys to kind of, you know, work together on that. >> I know you mentioned Kristen's vers versatility does like I guess when you're first installing, I mean, does he project as as a guy playing the same position as God actually, or is that just something he'll do on occasion? We got we got to let them go and you know, we'll we'll make those adjustments as we go, but uh what we feel like is we're bringing a really really talented player, really good person for our locker room into a group that um will provide some depth. You know, certainly, you know, it's it's hard to acquire big guys and so uh we'll add them to that mix and we'll kind of see how it goes. Can you make some acquisitions that you guys might like in free agency and the first few picks on offense allows you guys to be like maybe a little bit more versatile than you guys were last year in terms of personal package wanted to play more 12 or 11 or just be a little bit more how you see that? >> Yeah, I think that's a fair assessment. I think we do feel like we have a lot of guys who hey, they got a lot of versatility. They're really smart football players. Um, you know, more time together uh through this whole process and so uh all that stuff will build. seem pretty excited about the idea of lining up next to Brian Brazie was kind of assessment of, you know, how those two can complement one another. >> Yeah, I think we're adding them to a group that, um, has, you know, a nice mix. There's some veterans in there. Uh, Shep, God, uh, but then some young guys, you know, and some young guys. And so, um, you know, we're going to need a number of those guys. This is a uh tough hard business. This is the NFL. Uh there's nothing easy about it. The players individually are going to go through highs and lows. Uh, you know, for these guys, I mean, all these guys have had such a, you know, amazing one-of-a-kind ride to get to the position that they're in. So, um I grew up watching college football. Uh obviously I watched the Falcons here and there, but you know, I was never losing sleep over them. >> Yeah. Oscar, how would you just kind of describe your mentality as a as a blocker? You kind of just described as like the you playing a lot of why in in that offense there and like what was your approach in that area of your game? Yeah, I mean, um, I think it's the most important thing you can do as a tight end is be able to block and bring that to your game. Um, I love just being able to dominate another man and, um, in a successful offense, you have a tight end that could usually dominate the perimeter and own the C gap. So, I take pride in it and I enjoy it. >> You said you've known Christian since 8th grade. How did y'all cross paths prior to Georgia, >> man? Just camps everywhere. Um, in high school, we went to the some camps together and played in the All-American Bowl together. and he's always been a character. You know, everyone in Georgia always plays against each other at some point and crosses paths at some point. So, it's been awesome. And, uh, you know, we've been very close friends there since he got to Georgia. >> What was your best memories in the Sugar Bowl? Y'all spent some time here. Did you get a chance to kind of experience the city a little bit? Yeah, I mean just being on Biata, you know, um just walking around like I guess since it's a big bowl game, there are a lot of Georgia fans everywhere there, but the streets were always alive, fans so passionate, you still see all the Saints fans everywhere and everyone just walking around. Um Trevor Eten's a good buddy of mine who's from there and he was kind of showing me around everything and all the food and I'm excited to eat some of that food down there. So, uh it's it's just going to be a great place. You know anything about uh Jordan Tyson? >> Oh yeah, I do. He's a baller. Trained out there with him in uh um Arizona for the past couple months and uh you know he's a baller. Great dude to be around. Great kid. Super funny, super awesome. Uh, I've only got to hang out with them for a couple months, but I feel like we got a bond

transcripts.title: Saints HC Kellen Moore discusses selecting DT Christen Miller and TE Oscar Delp on Day 2
transcripts.text: All right, guys. Um, we got two Georgia Bulldogs today. So, quite the coincidence there. Uh, turned out pretty well for us. Obviously, uh, I'll just start with some highlights. Uh, you know, drafting Christian in the second round. Um, you know, four-year player at Georgia. Uh, two-year starter. Um, as we went through this process, we had a formal interview with him at the combine. Um, Peter Surman actually worked him out at Georgia. Uh, funny story there. was supposed to go, but the uh TSA issues at the uh airport kind of created a bit little bit of an issue there. So, Peter happened to be somewhere else close by and he hopped in the car and drove over there and worked him out. And so, uh it all worked out. But great player, love his energy, love his juice. I think you guys already sense that and kind of his media obligation so far. His versatility and his play style is going to be really good for us. And so, uh great move there. And then Oscar Del in the third round. Um you know, we had a formal interview with Oscar at the combine. He kind of shared I think a little bit of that. Josh Hill went and worked him out and so we got exposure to both these guys. Felt really comfortable with that through this whole process. He's a multi- spot guy.
